_doc: Learning paths (issue #309): short tours through the demos for one audience, read by the Pi (rq_learning_paths.sh: raspi-config -> Quantum Demos -> Learning paths, and the desktop icon) and by the website (scripts/generate-demo-list.js on gh-pages writes the Learning paths page). Fields per path: id (a-z, 0-9, -), title, audience, minutes, goal (one line), maturity ("beta" while new), steps (2-6), and for a path taken from someone else credit (one line) and credit_url. A step names what to start: demo (a manifest id, with an optional variant id), or command (an rq_*.sh tool in /usr/bin, for My Quantum Programs), or url (an outside page); name (optional for a demo, which then uses its manifest name; required for command and url); try and notice (one short line each, plain ASCII: whiptail shows them). A step in doQumentation on this Pi (demo qiskit-tutorials) may name page (its path there, e.g. /guides/quick-start), online (the same material on the web, offered when doQumentation is not downloaded or does not start) and time (the source's estimate, e.g. "1 hour"). ibm_learning (Continue with IBM Quantum Learning: title, text, url, and paths with slug, name, text and url) lists IBM Quantum's learning paths; the Pi offers it in the list and in Keep going, and the website as its own section; .github/workflows/ibm-learning-paths.yml compares the slugs with IBM's page weekly. next (2-3 entries, shown as Keep going after the last step): name, url and why (one short line), or path (the id of another path) and why. ladder (Where to go next, six rungs): rung, text (one short line) and links (1-4, each name and url, with an optional note: a sentence that names it). tests/unit/test_learning_paths.py checks all of this.

paths.title: First 15 minutes
paths.goal: Light up the panel, see a qubit and lose a coin game to a quantum computer.

steps.name: IBM LED Demo
steps.try: Look at the model: the IBM logo lights up on the LED panel.
steps.notice: The LEDs are the model's display: other demos, like RasQ-LED, show qubits on them.

steps.try: Press H: the arrow moves from the top of the sphere to the equator.
steps.notice: On the equator the qubit is in a superposition: 0 and 1 are equally likely.

steps.name: Quantum Coin Game
steps.try: Play heads or tails against a quantum computer: run each cell with Shift+Enter.
steps.notice: The quantum computer wins every game. Its trick is the H gate you just saw.

next.why: Find out what the H gate did to the coin.

next.name: Fun with Quantum
next.why: Play the quantum games at home, in your browser.

next.name: QAMPoser
next.why: Build your own quantum circuits in the browser.

paths.title: Superposition & measurement
paths.goal: Learn what a superposition is and what a measurement does to it.

steps.try: Press H: the arrow lies on the equator. Press H again: it is back at the top.
steps.notice: The bar shows the chance of 0. A measurement gives 0 or 1, never both.

steps.name: Quantum Coin Game
steps.try: Play the classical game first, then the quantum one with the H gate.
steps.notice: Two H gates bring the coin back to heads, whatever the other player did.

steps.name: Hardy's Paradox
steps.try: Follow the quantum cars and run each cell with Shift+Enter.
steps.notice: Everyday logic fails: you cannot reason about a measurement that did not happen.

next.name: Quantum mechanics module
next.why: Lessons on superposition, measurement and uncertainty, with Qiskit code.

next.name: Basics of quantum information
next.why: The full course: qubits, measurements and gates, at your own pace.
See what happens when two or three qubits share one state.

paths.title: Entanglement
paths.goal: Win games that no classical team can win every time, with entangled qubits.

steps.name: GHZ Game
steps.try: Look for a strategy that always wins, then let the quantum team play.
steps.notice: No classical strategy wins every round. Three entangled qubits do.

steps.name: Mermin–Peres Magic Square
steps.try: Look for a magic square that works, then run the quantum strategy for many rounds.
steps.notice: Alice's and Bob's answers are random, yet they always agree where they meet.

steps.try: Just watch: it entangles blocks of 1, 2, 3 ... qubits, up to the whole panel, and measures.
steps.notice: Block size 1: random colours. In an entangled block every LED shows the same: red or blue.

next.name: CHSH inequality tutorial
next.why: Run a Bell test on a real quantum computer.

next.name: Entanglement in action
next.why: Teleportation, superdense coding and the CHSH game, step by step.
Write your own entangled circuit with Qiskit.

paths.title: Your first program
paths.goal: Write and run a quantum circuit with Qiskit, then keep learning.

steps.name: My Quantum Programs
steps.try: Hello-World.ipynb opens: run its cells one by one with Shift+Enter.
steps.notice: Two entangled qubits: you measure 00 or 11, never 01 or 10.

steps.try: Open Tutorials, then Hello World, and click Run All: the code runs on this Pi.
steps.notice: The circuit from step 1, explained step by step, with more tutorials and courses next to it.

steps.name: IBM Quantum Learning
steps.try: Take a free course, for example Basics of quantum information.
steps.notice: It needs the internet. With an IBM Quantum account your code runs on real quantum computers.

next.name: Qiskit 101 hands-on
next.why: A workshop notebook: your first circuits, a quiz and a run on real hardware.

next.name: Fundamentals of quantum algorithms
next.why: Query algorithms, phase estimation, factoring and Grover's search.

next.name: CertiQ
next.why: Free community prep for the Qiskit developer certification (unofficial, not by IBM).

paths.title: IBM: Introduction to quantum
paths.goal: Learn key terms, applications and starter skills, on this Pi where you can.
paths.credit: From IBM Quantum Learning: its Introduction to quantum learning path.

steps.name: Quickstart
steps.try: Skip Install Qiskit (it is on this Pi): build the circuit and run its cells.
steps.notice: A few lines of code build a circuit, draw it and show its results.

steps.name: Run your first circuit on hardware
steps.try: Follow its four steps: map, optimize, execute, analyze. Hardware needs an IBM Quantum account.
steps.notice: The same four steps run every Qiskit program, from two qubits to over a hundred.

steps.name: IBM Quantum Composer
steps.try: Read the guide, then build a circuit in the Composer (online, IBM Quantum account).
steps.notice: The Composer draws circuits by drag and drop and shows their Qiskit code.

steps.name: Quantum computing in practice
steps.try: Seven lessons: start with the introduction, one lesson at a time.
steps.notice: What quantum computers can do today, and how a problem gets onto one.

steps.name: Basics of quantum information
steps.try: Start with Single systems. Take your time: each lesson builds on the last.
steps.notice: The ideas behind every other step: qubits, measurements, gates, entanglement.

steps.name: CHSH inequality
steps.try: Run it on real hardware with an IBM Quantum account.
steps.notice: Entangled qubits break a limit no classical system can. It fails in Simulator mode for now.

next.name: Introduction to quantum at IBM
next.why: The same path online: earn its badge with an IBM Quantum account.
